storyPreview.title: The Brass Bell Conspiracy
storyPreview.summary: When the newly restored fog bell of Gullmarsh Harbor rings twelve times on a windless night, the town wakes to find its beloved tidewarden missing and the harbor’s famous pearl ledger stolen from a locked counting room. SirLocked and a trusted companion must follow salt-stained clues, conflicting alibis, and a trail of old grudges through a close-knit seaside community where everyone heard the bell, but no one agrees on what it meant.
storyPreview.setting: Gullmarsh Harbor, a rain-polished coastal town built around crooked piers, lantern-lit alleys, oyster boats, and an aging lighthouse. The case unfolds over one stormy evening and the gray morning after, with four investigation-focused scenes designed for cooperative clue sharing and cross-checking testimony.
storyPreview.openingIncident: During the Founders’ Tide festival, the ceremonial brass fog bell rings out from the locked bellhouse despite no scheduled signal and no keeper on duty. Moments later, the tidewarden’s office is discovered in disarray, the pearl ledger is gone, and the tidewarden has vanished, leaving only a wet footprint, a torn festival ribbon, and a room full of witnesses who all claim to have been elsewhere.
storyPreview.tone: Atmospheric, clever, and suspenseful without being grim. Expect maritime folklore, village secrets, puzzling physical evidence, and suspects with sympathetic motives as well as suspicious behavior.
storyPreview.playerPromise: Players will compare witness timelines, inspect locked-room oddities, decode harbor customs, and split investigative attention between public festival events and hidden waterfront dealings. The mystery is fair-play and medium difficulty, rewarding cooperation between SirLocked and the companion as they connect environmental clues with social deductions.
keyLocations: The locked bellhouse above Gullmarsh Pier
The tidewarden’s ledger office beside the customs scale
The lantern market during the Founders’ Tide festival
The old lighthouse causeway at low tide
suspectTeasers: A pearl merchant whose fortunes depend on what the missing ledger contains
A festival musician seen near the pier shortly before the bell rang
The assistant tidewarden, eager for promotion and strangely calm about the disappearance
A retired lighthouse keeper who insists the bell was warning the town, not summoning it
A boatwright with unpaid debts and fresh tar on their cuffs
